summary: This Wikipedia article covers the 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament, a 68-team single-elimination event deciding the 2017-18 college basketball national champion. The 80th edition began March 13, 2018, and ended with the championship game on April 2 at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas. Villanova beat Michigan for its third title, and the note highlights new arenas and venues used that year, including Philips Arena, Little Caesars Arena and Intrust Bank Arena.
one_line: The 2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament, an 80th-edition 68-team event in which Villanova won its third national title over Michigan.
key_facts: The 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament was a 68-team single-elimination tournament.
The tournament determined the NCAA Division I men's college basketball national champion for the 2017-18 season.
The 80th edition of the tournament began on March 13, 2018.
The championship game was played on April 2, 2018, at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas.
The Alamodome hosted the Final Four for the fourth time.
The 2018 tournament was the first since 1994 in which no games were played in an NFL stadium.
Philips Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks and replacement for the Omni Coliseum, hosted the South regional games.
Little Caesars Arena, home of the Detroit Pistons and Detroit Red Wings, hosted games in 2018.
Intrust Bank Arena in Wichita, Kansas hosted first round games, the first time the tournament returned to Wichita and Kansas since 1994.
Villanova Wildcats won the championship, their 3rd title and 4th title game appearance.
Michigan Wolverines were runner-up, their 7th title game appearance and 8th Final Four.
Kansas Jayhawks reached the Final Four for the 15th time.
Loyola-Chicago Ramblers reached the Final Four for the 2nd time.
Jay Wright won his 2nd national title as Villanova's winning coach.
Donte DiVincenzo of Villanova was named the Most Outstanding Player.
